text:
sara-support: FYI — ACME reported a streaming response that ended without the final JSON object and no finish_reason. Happens when their client rotates credentials mid-stream. Repro steps and logs below, please triage.

ashley-client: Repro from their side: long generation (~45s), we triggered a key rotate for the org (server-side rotation) ~30s in. Client sees last chunk trimmed and parser fails on trailing comma. No 5xx or error, just connection close.

ashley-client: curl we used to repro: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream -d '{"prompt": "long...", "max_tokens": 1200}'
```

ashley-client: client logs (abridged):
```
[00:30:12] SSE: event: chunk data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...\n"}}]}
[00:30:41] AUTH: rotate start (org=acme)
[00:30:41] SSE: connection re-established, resume-id=xyz123
[00:30:41] SSE: event: chunk data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}]},
[00:30:41] SSE: connection closed (200)
```
They see trailing comma after the last object and no `{"finish_reason":...}` or final sentinel.

devin-engineer: Thanks — I think this is the resume/auth-handoff edge. Two hypotheses: 1) our reconnect path drops/short-circuits the final flush that emits the closing object/sentinel; 2) the client resume merges partial last-event boundaries and the intermediary comma remains.

devin-engineer: Quick checks: can you grab the raw wire dump for the initial connection and the resumed connection (including headers for resume-id, x-request-id)? Also which SDK they used (node/fetch/browser)?

ashley-client: They used our internal Node SDK (fetch-based) on a server. Raw dump attached (excerpt above). resume-id header present on rejoin. No 401 observed; rotation was server-initiated on auth service, client didn't explicitly refresh mid-request.

devin-engineer: Repro locally with a scripted auth-rotate: I could reproduce truncated tail when rotation triggered a short reconnect where the server returned a 200 on the reconnect, but the final sentinel was emitted on the previous connection's flush path. Server GC closed the prior socket before the final sentinel made the outbound write.

devin-engineer: Short-term mitigation: ensure clients tolerate trailing commas or treat the stream as newline-delimited JSON fragments rather than a strict single JSON array/object. Long-term we should guarantee an end-sentinel on any reconnect/close.

tim-ops: Severity? Customer blocked in production. They rely on strict JSON assembly. Marking P1 for support escalation. @devin-engineer can you propose a patch and a safe rollback plan?

devin-engineer: Proposal: on auth handoff/reconnect flow, add a server-side buffered flush that emits an explicit terminal event before socket teardown if any partial event queued. Also change resume logic to include a final 'end_of_response' sentinel emitted by the origin that the resume handler will forward if it hasn't been consumed. Patch: add call to connection.flush_final_event() in auth-handshake cleanup. Rollout: canary to hosted region us-west-2 for 15m, monitor 5xx and streaming finish_rate metric. If finish_rate drops, rollback.

sara-support: Sounds good. Also requested customer-side workaround: upgrade Node SDK to v0.9.3 which tolerates trailing commas (parsing fallback) and implements a 250ms drain wait before declaring a stream closed.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created: https://deploys.redwood.ai/req/6152 — canary to us-west-2, owner=devin-engineer, eta=30m.

tim-ops: Need logs from the host that closed the socket (proxy vs origin). Devin, please add logging for "flush_final_event emitted=true|false" and include resume-id in logs.

devin-engineer: Will do. Adding metric finish_sentinel_emitted{region,model,org} and an alert if <99.9% over 5m.

ashley-client: Customer accepted the SDK workaround for now. They've asked for postmortem and timeline once fix deployed.

sara-support: Assigning follow-ups: @devin-engineer (patch + canary + metrics), @tim-ops (monitoring + escalation), @ashley-client (customer comms). I'll keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
